high.title: USD and Oil Prices Surge Due to Middle East Conflict: How Will Exchange Rates and Inflation in Vietnam Be Affected?
high.summary: Following escalating Middle East tensions after US-Israel strikes on Iran on February 28, 2026, global financial markets experienced significant volatility. The USD Index (DXY) immediately jumped 0.8% to 98.42 points, while oil prices surged amid supply disruption concerns. Gold prices also rose, reflecting a clear "risk-off" sentiment in global markets. According to VCBS analysis, this geopolitical uncertainty is driving capital flows toward safe-haven assets like USD and gold. For Vietnam, this creates multiple pressures: stronger USD could weaken VND, while higher oil prices may fuel imported inflation. The combination threatens Vietnam's inflation targets and could force SBV intervention to stabilize the exchange rate. Key risks include supply chain disruptions increasing logistics costs, potential capital outflows from emerging markets like Vietnam, and imported inflation from higher energy costs. Investors should monitor VND/USD closely for potential SBV intervention signals and watch for any shifts in monetary policy stance if inflationary pressures intensify.

high.title: VN-Index Lost Over 113 Points in One Week, Experts Identify Stock Groups in "Oversold Territory"
high.summary: The Vietnamese stock market closed the first week of March with negative performance as VN-Index plummeted to its lowest level in three weeks. The index closed at 1,767 points on March 6, losing over 40 points from the previous session and over 113 points for the week - a sharp decline similar to the "tariff shock" in April 2025. Selling pressure intensified amid escalating Middle East geopolitical tensions, causing investor anxiety. Except for sectors benefiting from oil price movements like petroleum, chemicals, and maritime transport, most stock groups were in red. Experts note that while oil & gas and related sectors gained from higher crude prices, banking, real estate, and consumer stocks suffered heavy losses. The market selloff reflects global risk-off sentiment as investors flee emerging market equities. For FX traders, this equity outflow pressure could weaken VND as foreign investors potentially repatriate funds. Watch for potential SBV intervention if selling pressure continues and threatens currency stability.

medium.title: MB Bank Just Strongly Increased Savings Interest Rates
medium.summary: MB Bank significantly raised deposit rates for terms of 12 months and longer. The 12-18 month rates increased from 5.5% to 6.1% annually (up 0.6 percentage points), while 24-60 month terms rose from 6.3% to 6.6% annually (up 0.3 points). Short-term rates under 12 months remained unchanged. This rate hike suggests increasing competition for deposits among Vietnamese banks and could signal broader monetary tightening pressures if other banks follow suit.

medium.title: BIDV Interest Rates March 2025: Which Term Has the Highest Interest Rate?
medium.summary: BIDV maintains stable deposit rates in early March 2026, with highest rates of 5.3% annually for 24-36 month terms. Short-term rates remain at 2.1% for 1-2 months, while 12-month deposits offer 5.2% annually. The stable rate structure contrasts with MB Bank's recent increases, suggesting differentiated competitive strategies among major Vietnamese banks for deposit mobilization.

medium.title: Vietcombank Latest Interest Rates March 2026
medium.summary: Vietcombank continues maintaining stable deposit rates in early March 2026, with maximum rates of 5.3% annually for terms of 24 months and longer. The bank applies uniform rates for both counter and online deposits. Short-term rates remain at 2.1% for 1-2 months and 5.2% for 12-month deposits, showing consistency with other major state-owned banks like BIDV.

medium.title: Good News for All Citizens Borrowing from Banks and Financial Companies
medium.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam is seeking public comments on draft regulations that would raise the threshold for "small-value loans" from 100 million VND to 400 million VND for credit institutions (200 million VND for People's Credit Funds). This regulatory change would allow borrowers of amounts under these thresholds to avoid providing detailed capital usage plans, significantly simplifying the loan application process for consumers and small businesses.
